## Samsung Electronics wins $200 billion Broadcom AI chip partnership, boosting foundry push against TSMC

A $200B, multi-year foundry commitment from Broadcom is the clearest evidence yet that Samsung can contest TSMC for advanced AI chip volumes; for AVGO holders, it signals foundry supply diversification, while for TSM holders it raises questions about medium-term share concentration.

- Samsung Electronics and Broadcom have signed an AI chip partnership reported at $200 billion in value.
- One headline specifies the deal runs through 2030, representing a long-duration volume commitment.
- Three independent outlets confirm the deal, with framing consistently emphasizing Samsung's foundry ambitions vs. TSMC.
- Broadcom (AVGO) is the customer; Samsung is the manufacturing partner.
- No per-year volume, process node, or chip category specifics are present in the headlines.
